desks.Dividends: Apple goes ex-dividend Thu Nov 12 at $0.27 per quarter, unchanged from August and the third payment at that rate; Microsoft goes ex-dividend Thu Nov 19 at $0.98, the first payment at the raised rate (+7.7% from $0.91, its 24th consecutive annual increase), payable Dec 10. Nvidia's next ex-date is not yet declared, and the Dec 10 date listed by one source contradicts Nasdaq's calendar, so it is UNVERIFIED. SPY and QQQ December distributions are pattern-based estimates, not declarations. Tesla pays no dividend.
desks.Earnings: Nvidia is the only watchlist name reporting in the window, Tue Nov 17 after close, with Nasdaq consensus EPS of $2.49 (13 estimates), confirmed by the company release; the Nov 20 straddle implies about 12.5%, up from 9.0% yesterday as the stock fell 9.26% to $181.60. Apple reported Mon Nov 2 after close with revenue of $114.5 billion, up 12% year over year, and EPS of $2.10; its first-session reaction was -1.9% on Nov 3. Microsoft reported Oct 28 and Tesla reported Oct 21.
desks.Futures: The EIA petroleum report released Wed Nov 4 showed crude drawing 865,000 barrels against a Reuters poll expecting an 877,000-barrel build, and distillate drawing 3.6 million barrels to 99.3 million, the lowest since May 2003 and 13% below its five-year average, yet Brent fell 8.7% to $94.62 and WTI 8.3% to $88.12 on midterm results and Iran de-escalation hopes. Claims of tanker strikes in the Strait of Hormuz are single-source state-media reports and UNVERIFIED. Natural gas storage rose 77 billion cubic feet to 3,801 billion, versus a survey of 81 and a five-year average build of 61. Next catalysts: USDA WASDE and EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook Tue Nov 10.
desks.Parity: No published put-call or box parity violation was found for the watchlist. S&P Dow Jones Indices announced a revision to its growth/value classification rules, effective at the annual reconstitution before the open on Dec 21, with pro forma files Dec 4: growth drops 12-month price momentum, value moves to an intangibles-adjusted measure plus earnings- and free-cash-flow-to-price. The change is to style classification, not index membership or parity math, and is a watch item for the growth-heavy watchlist names. FTSE Russell is separately consulting on its growth/value split, closing Dec 11.
desks.Premium: Live 29-day implied volatility prints are SPY 21.5%, QQQ 33.9%, Apple 28.2%, Microsoft 33.0%, Nvidia 63.0%, and Tesla 56.1%. One-day index prints are UNRELIABLE: SPY and QQQ call-minus-put mids violate put-call parity at the same strike, so the one-day means are not clean levels. Every implied-versus-realized verdict is WINDOW-CONTINGENT: once today's returns enter the 20-day window, realized volatility jumps to about 21% for SPY, 33% for QQQ, 47% for Nvidia, and 57% for Tesla, and the apparent premium compresses to about 0-2 points. Nvidia's 29-day print spans the Nov 17 earnings date and is event premium, not a richness signal. Implied-volatility rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names.
desks.Quant lab: Seven new candidates were added to the ledger (#207-213), all scored WATCH or ARCHIVE, with no TEST or INTEGRATE movement. The strongest is #207, 'Hard to Fool: A Bounded LLM Research Loop for Quantitative Finance' (score 57, WATCH), a strict holdout-once research loop whose headline failure is a strategy at Sharpe about 3 in discovery and validation falling to 0.26 on its single holdout use. Its code link is present but repo contents and license were not verified this run, as the GitHub leg was skipped. The other papers form a methods cluster with it on frozen referees and anytime-valid promotion tests.

headline: Daily research brief — Thursday, November 5

items.detail: SPY closed -4.41%, QQQ -6.49%, Nvidia -9.26%, and Tesla -10.77% on Nov 5. Once today's returns enter the 20-day realized-volatility window, realized volatility jumps to about 21% for SPY, 33% for QQQ, 47% for Nvidia, and 57% for Tesla, with a single day driving 46-63% of each window's variance. The apparent premium over realized volatility (+8 to +17 points on the window through Nov 4) compresses to about 0-2 points, so every implied-versus-realized verdict this run is WINDOW-CONTINGENT.

items.detail: The EIA report released Wed Nov 4 showed crude drawing 865,000 barrels against an expected build, and distillate at 99.3 million barrels, its lowest since May 2003 and 13% below its five-year average, yet Brent fell 8.7% to $94.62 and WTI 8.3% to $88.12. items.title: Crude fell more than 8% into bullish inventory data

items.detail: FRED prints dated Nov 4, the latest available, put the effective fed funds rate at 3.88%, the 2-year at 4.58%, and the 10-year at 4.90%, a 2s10s spread of +32 basis points, down from a 47-basis-point peak in early October. SOFR at 3.94% sits 6 basis points over the effective fed funds rate, a normal overnight funding print with no stress signal. The 10-year has eased 41 basis points since Oct 5, which modestly relieves discount-rate pressure on growth names, but near 5% it remains a valuation headwind for long-duration exposure.
items.title: Rates: 10-year at 4.90%, curve flattening, funding calm
